Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has added a slightly longer front‑wing flap and reshaped the front‑corner air scoop, giving the car a steadier, more planted front end. The bigger, re‑profiled intake also helps keep temperatures in check, so the car can run its optimal settings without worrying about overheating. Together, these tweaks should improve cornering grip and reliability, giving the team a better shot at extracting maximum performance this weekend.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin rolled out a sharper, more aggressive front‑wing flap tailored to the track’s demands, building on the new wing they debuted last race. The extra bite at the front gives the car more front‑end grip, helping it turn into corners quicker and stay balanced through high‑speed sections—exactly the edge needed to fight for points this weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has tweaked the front‑corner of the car, smoothing the surface to keep the airflow steadier as it rolls through the bends, which should give the driver a bit more grip and confidence out of the turns. They’ve also fitted a bigger cooling louvre, tuned for this circuit’s hot‑track demands, so the engine stays in its optimal temperature window longer. Together, the aerodynamic refinement and extra cooling aim to boost corner‑speed and reliability for the weekend’s sprint.
